---
title: Nested Sidebar
---

This example has **two sidebars**, each rooted in its own
subdirectory:

- The **User Guide** sidebar covers pages under `guide/`. It
  contains nested `Getting Started` and `Advanced` sections.
- The **Reference** sidebar covers pages under `reference/`. It is
  flat.

Quarto picks the right sidebar for the page being rendered by
looking at which sidebar's contents reference the current source
path. There is no per-page configuration — the containment is
implicit.

Visit the [User Guide](guide/index.qmd) or the
[Reference](reference/index.qmd) to see them in action. As you move
between the two subtrees, the sidebar swaps. Each page also gets a
**prev / next** strip at the bottom, derived from the resolved
sidebar's flattened order.

## What this page sees

This top-level `index.qmd` does **not** belong to either sidebar's
contents, so neither sidebar applies. The page renders without one.
That's a useful corner of the design: the same code path produces
"no sidebar" without a special flag.
